'Has derivative' is functional..why: The derivative of a differentiable function is a single function (the one that maps each point to the derivative's value there); Wikipedia defines 'the derivative function' with the definite article. Calculus texts say it constantly (the derivative of sin x is cos x) and never speak of two competing derivatives.

sources.quote: If f is a function that has a derivative at every point in its domain, then a function can be defined by mapping every point x to the value of the derivative of f at x. This function is written f′ and is called the derivative function or the derivative of f.

sources.query: the derivative of a function is unique
a function has a unique derivative

A right angle measures 90 degrees..why: The first sentence of the Right angle article.

sources.quote: In geometry and trigonometry, a right angle is an angle of exactly 90 degrees or π/2 radians corresponding to a quarter turn.

A right angle measures 60 degrees..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: a right angle is 90 degrees.

sources.quote: In geometry and trigonometry, a right angle is an angle of exactly 90 degrees or π/2 radians corresponding to a quarter turn.

notes: RBox contraction (functional) paired with mathematics-replace-0011: removes the functionality of 'has derivative'. Uniqueness of the derivative is a theorem, not a definition, so there is nothing to restore. The instance questions use letters and the indefinite 'a derivative of', so the prompt does not presuppose uniqueness. The first instance asks whether the two could differ (no before), the second whether they must be equal (yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. The not query asks the possibility the removal opens ('can have two different derivative functions', no). Side facts about right angles are copied from the revision. Unrelated near is functionality of another relation (a real number has one cube; answer no to two cubes), which a leak would turn to an abstention. Caveat: a model may keep uniqueness of the derivative as mathematical knowledge. hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
